label: The catalog validator discards the :line/:line-end suffix before every anchor check, in SOURCE FILES cells and in prose paths alike, so catalog code anchors are only tested for whole-file existence; the corpora cite line ranges heavily, so the lightest anchor check is to retain the suffix and resolve it through the already-exported resolveCitation (or the --advise shell-out validate_document.py already uses), failing past_end/moved_past_end/unresolved.

No existing check extracts CLI flags from scenario command blocks (targeted search negative), and the playbook package ships no runner; the lightest option check is static: extract --flag tokens from fenced commands, identify the invoked script, and require each flag to be a case label of that script, mirroring the unknown-option rejection the 018 fix installed in create.sh at runtime.

Expected answers can be anchored as literal tokens: distinctive literals in a scenario's Expected block (PROVIDE-DESCRIPTIVE-SLUG, the [speckit] Warning prefix) must exist in the producing script named by the scenario's Commands block, and both exemplar literals do exist in create.sh, so a literal-presence check modeled on validate-doc-model-refs.js is the lightest partial test of expected answers against code.

cite-drift-scan.mjs is report-only: main() prints a census and returns 0, and --advise returns 0 unless the invocation is bad, so any drift gate must be a consumer that interprets verdicts; check-source-tags-helper.mjs is that consumer shape, importing the resolver, emitting WARN records and exiting 0.

The playbook package contains only the validator and templates with no command runner, so the lightest self-check for scenarios must be static extraction and resolution rather than executing the scenario corpus, reinforcing iteration 1's ruled-out direction.
A citation check that strips the :line/:line-end suffix before resolution cannot detect anchor drift; the suffix is the anchor and must survive to the bounds or verdict test.

Static option checking is only defined where a scenario names a repository script; steps that invoke skills or agents (slash-command steps, agent: steps) have no option surface and are outside any flag check's reach.

check-source-tags-helper.mjs imports CITATION_RE, FENCE_RE, listTrackedFiles, loadRedirects and resolveCitation straight from sk-doc's scanner, so a second consumer can reuse the resolution logic without new machinery.

validate_document.py already shells cite-drift-scan.mjs --advise per document and only appends advisory lines, so the playbook/catalog anchor path could reuse an existing invocation pattern but is advisory today.

direction: Reuse the citation scanner for command-block flags: make cite-drift-scan read fenced blocks or match --flag tokens
reason: The scanner deliberately skips fenced content and matches path:line citations only; forcing it into command blocks would either misread shell text as citations or duplicate its resolver in a second, worse extractor. Flags need a dedicated extraction path with the invoked script as the canonical option source.

direction: Parse the usage()/help text of each script as the canonical option set for the flag check
reason: Help text is prose that can drift from the parser; the case labels are the executable truth and are already the contract the runtime enforces, so the check resolves against the parser branches instead.
